headline: Typhoon Dolphin Makes Landfall on China's Zhejiang-Fujian Coast as Fuego Volcano Eruption Forces Mass Evacuations in Guatemala
overview: Typhoon Dolphin has struck the Chinese coastline between Zhejiang and Fujian provinces, bringing destructive winds and heavy rain to one of China's most densely populated coastal corridors. Simultaneously, Guatemala's Fuego volcano erupted with its highest alert in years, while a multi-continent heat emergency continues across Europe and the central United States. An unusually widely-felt M5.6 earthquake near Anchorage, Alaska, rounds out a globally active natural hazard picture on August 9.

events.title: Typhoon Dolphin Makes Landfall on China's Zhejiang-Fujian Coast
events.summary: Typhoon Dolphin has made landfall along the coast between Zhejiang and Fujian provinces, a track meteorologists are calling exceptionally rare given that the storm formed near the International Date Line. Shanghai recorded 83.4 mm of rainfall in a single day — consistent with the typhoon's outer rainbands sweeping across the Yangtze Delta. Fishing fleets were ordered back to port days in advance, and millions of coastal residents are under evacuation or shelter-in-place orders as the storm moves inland.

events.title: Fuego Volcano Erupts in Guatemala — Second-Highest National Alert Issued
events.summary: Guatemala's Fuego volcano erupted on August 4, prompting authorities to issue the country's second-highest danger alert and ordering evacuations of communities within the volcano's hazard zones approximately 65 km southwest of Guatemala City. The eruption lasted approximately 50 hours, with lava flows, pyroclastic material, and ash forcing thousands to flee before Guatemalan authorities declared the eruption over on August 6 and allowed evacuees to begin returning home. Fuego remains one of Central America's most persistently active volcanoes and is under continued monitoring.

events.title: M5.6 Earthquake Near Skwentna Widely Felt Across South-Central Alaska
events.summary: A magnitude 5.6 earthquake struck approximately 57 km west-northwest of Skwentna, Alaska, at a shallow depth of 10 km on August 8, making it one of the most widely felt seismic events in the region in recent years, with over 1,133 felt reports submitted to USGS — a remarkably high number for a sub-M6.0 event. The shallow focal depth amplified shaking across the Matanuska-Susitna Borough and as far as Anchorage, roughly 107 miles to the southeast. No tsunami alert was issued and USGS assigned a green alert level, indicating low likelihood of significant damage, though the event is under continued watch given the active seismic environment.

events.title: Europe Heatwave Expands West — France, UK, and Germany Now in the Heat Corridor
events.location: France, United Kingdom, Germany, and Central Europe
events.summary: The relentless European heatwave has expanded decisively westward, with Paris reaching 32.8°C, London 31.8°C, and Berlin 31.6°C — conditions well above seasonal norms for early August and adding millions more to the heat-stressed population. This marks a significant escalation from the prior days when extreme heat was concentrated in Italy, Austria, and Slovakia; the westward push now places France and the UK under serious heat strain, straining energy grids, transport infrastructure, and public health systems. Italy remains on its highest alert, and drought conditions fueled by the heatwave are raising additional concerns across the continent.

events.title: Missouri and Midwest Extreme Heat Warning Extended Through August 12
events.location: Missouri, Kansas, and Southern Illinois, USA
events.summary: The National Weather Service has formally upgraded heat watches to Extreme Heat Warnings across a broad swath of Missouri, Kansas, and southern Illinois, with heat index values expected to reach 107–109°F daily through Wednesday, August 12. Overnight lows remaining in the upper 70s to lower 80s are providing little physiological relief, compounding the multi-day heat stress risk for vulnerable populations. The warnings — issued simultaneously from NWS offices in St. Louis, Springfield, and Kansas City — represent one of the most geographically extensive Midwest heat emergencies in recent years.

events.title: India Monsoon Floods and Landslides — Death Toll Surpasses 100
events.location: Kerala, Delhi, and Multiple States, India
events.summary: Monsoon-driven floods and landslides have killed more than 100 people across India since July, with Kerala and Delhi among the hardest-hit regions as relentless rainfall overwhelms drainage systems, triggers slope failures, and inundates low-lying communities. Kerala has been particularly devastated, with landslides cutting off villages and rescue teams wading through floodwaters to reach stranded residents; Delhi recorded dangerous flooding that disrupted the capital's transport network. Monsoon conditions remain active across the subcontinent with further rain forecast, keeping the disaster risk elevated.

events.title: US Wildfire Season — Red Flag Warnings Blanket the West and Southern Plains
events.location: Wyoming, Montana, Idaho, Washington, Oklahoma, and Western USA
events.summary: Red Flag Warnings remain active across a sweeping arc of the American West and Southern Plains on August 9, covering Yellowstone National Park, the Wyoming high country, eastern Washington Cascades, Idaho's Salmon River Mountains, and western Oklahoma — where relative humidity has dropped as low as 10–14% with gusts to 40 mph. These conditions sustain an extreme fire ignition and spread environment atop a wildfire season already tracking above the 10-year average with 99 large fires simultaneously active. With multiple major fires already burning in the Pacific Northwest and Northern Rockies, fire managers are warning that any new ignitions in Red Flag zones today could rapidly become uncontrollable.
